member.summary:
One branch of a ConcurrentCommands group: commands that run in order.
Maps to BranchType in XML-Profiles.xsd, which ConcurrentCommandsType does not use. Annex B.1 and Tables 8.15 and 8.16 of the specification give ConcurrentCommands a branch_list of branches, and OpenRoIS follows them (docs/rois-reference.md, section 16).
Attributes: command_list: The commands of the branch, run one after the other.

member.name: T:OpenRoIS.Interfaces.Hri.ConcurrentCommands
member.summary:
A group of branches executed in parallel.
Maps to ConcurrentCommandsType in XML-Profiles.xsd, with the branch_list of Annex B.1. The branches run at the same time, each branch runs its commands in order, and the next unit of the sequence waits for every branch.
The XSD form, a flat command_list, is read as one-command branches.
Attributes: branch_list: The branches to run in parallel. delay_time: Optional delay in milliseconds before executing this group.

An ordered sequence of command units (sequential and/or concurrent).
Maps to CommandUnitSequenceType in XML-Profiles.xsd. The IDL typedefs this as `string`, but the XSD defines a rich structure with sequential and concurrent branches. We model the structured form; the string representation is the wire serialization format.
Attributes: command_unit_list: Ordered list of command units and/or concurrent groups.

member.name: T:OpenRoIS.Interfaces.Profiles.ComponentFunction
member.summary:
The RoSO function class of a component.
Not part of XML-Profiles.xsd. The values are the Robotic Service Function Ontology classes that the spec's ontology file assigns to the basic components: Navigation, Reaction and SpeechSynthesis are Actuation, the detection, localization and recognition components are Sensing, and AudioStreaming is the generic Function class. An engine requires a bind before commands on an actuation component.
ACTUATION: The component acts on the world (moves, speaks, shows). SENSING: The component observes the world. FUNCTION: The component is neither, for example a stream.

Maps to HRIEngineProfileType in XML-Profiles.xsd, field for field. The profile names its components by ref only, as the XSD does. The get_profile result carries their HRIComponentProfiles next to it.
Attributes: identifier: The engine's structured identifier. name: The gml:name of the engine, or None when it has none. sub_profiles: One profile per child engine (XSD SubProfile). component_ids: Fully qualified refs of every component reachable through this engine, including the components of its child engines (XSD HRIComponent). parameter_profiles: Engine-level parameter declarations.

member.name: T:OpenRoIS.Interfaces.RoISValues
member.summary: How a typed RoIS value travels as a string, in Result.Value, Parameter.Value and Argument.Value.

remarks.para: Hand-written, not generated: JSON Schema describes data, not functions. This class mirrors the Python module openrois.interfaces.values, and the vectors in interfaces/fixtures/values.json and interfaces/fixtures/value-edges.json keep the two the same. Section 17 of docs/rois-reference.md describes the string forms.

item.description: A , or a beyond its range, written in decimal.
A , written as the shortest text that reads back as the same number, always with a fraction or an exponent (2.0, 1e-05).

item.term: string, RoISIdentifier, DateTime and any other type
item.description: A , written as the text itself. A or a is written in ISO 8601.
An object[] of that type, written as a JSON array.

remarks.para: Type names are matched without regard to case. An array holds its items as JSON values: numbers for the numeric types, true and false for the boolean types, and strings for every other type. NaN, Infinity and -Infinity stand bare in a float array, as Python writes them.

This class differs from Python on text that no writer produces. A number is read in ASCII digits only, where Python also reads other Unicode digits. An array item with a lone surrogate is refused, because System.Text.Json has no string for it. The item -0 of a float array reads as negative zero, where Python reads it as an integer and gives positive zero.
